items.title: Who's That
items.note: WBRU's first add that week; its big eighties sound was compared to the closing song of The Breakfast Club.

src.label: The 5 Best Songs Of The Week, Aug 7

items.title: From
items.note: Closing track from her album tiarn, recorded as a storm rolled into her Australian beach town; an ambient folk ballad, wistful and tender.

items.title: I Know!
items.note: Opening track of the debut album Mount Zero, with spindly guitars and a burrowing refrain.

items.title: Orchards
items.note: Second song on the follow-up, over delicate piano from Child Actor, arriving at tranquil acceptance.

items.title: The Big E
items.note: Title track and lead single from the album The Big E, about alien visitors, aging, and being misunderstood, with a frantic, unnerved energy.

items.title: Free Byrd
items.note: A winsome, characterful indie jangler about betting on yourself over a too-safe relationship, fulfilling its 'free' brief.

items.title: Scam Manifesto
items.note: Irish post-punks riff on Valerie Solanas's manifesto to address hypocrisy about beauty norms, with sludgy guitar and muttered self-recrimination.

items.title: Fabienk
items.note: Discussed as the big topic at the station's music meeting; described as hard to classify, current, nerdy, and almost danceable.

items.title: G.V.O.
items.note: Their first single in three years, an absurdist post-punk track with literary influences and art-rock energy, described as a joy to hear back.

src.label: Songs you need this week, Oct 21

items.title: Stratocaster
items.note: The crown jewel of Stick Around For Tea, with a sweetly chipper sound that hides an ache about expectations and refusing to play by rules.
